text: Yesterday, I visited a new city. I did not know the streets, so I asked a woman for directions to the hospital. She said, 'Go straight on this road, then turn left at the corner. The hospital is near the bank, not far from here.' I said thank you and started walking. There was a lot of traffic, so I waited for the light to turn green before I crossed the road. I walked past many shops and a big building. Then I saw a small park with a river and a bridge. I crossed the bridge and turned right. Finally, I saw the train station next to the hospital. The woman was right; it was not far. On my way back, I walked through the park again because I liked the trees and flowers there. Next time, I will remember the directions myself. I learned that streets in a new city can be confusing, but people are usually happy to help you find the right way. Asking for directions is a good idea when you are lost.
